finding.claim: POST /profile/avatar fetches a user-supplied URL server-side. The only check is that the string starts with "https://". There is no host or IP allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local blocklist, and no DNS-resolution check. An attacker can make the server request internal HTTPS services, such as https://users.internal, internal admin endpoints, or any host resolving to a private IP. An attacker-controlled public host can also 302-redirect to http://169.254.169.254/ or http://users.internal:8080/, because axios follows redirects by default (up to 5) and the scheme check is not re-applied to redirect targets. Response size is returned to the caller, which gives a blind/semi-blind oracle for internal reachability.

trace.note: Only validation: typeof string and startsWith("https://")
axios.get(url) issues the request, with redirects followed by default
Response body length is returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: The startsWith("https://") check blocks only non-https schemes (http, file, gopher) and does not constrain host. It is bypassable with internal HTTPS hosts, with redirects, and with hostnames that resolve to private IPs. No allowlist, IP-range filtering, maxRedirects: 0, or custom DNS-pinning agent is present. No authentication middleware is present.

verdict.guard_found: Only a scheme-prefix check, typeof string and url.startsWith("https://") at server.js:11. No host allowlist, IP blocklist, maxRedirects limit, or auth middleware.
verdict.reason: server.js:10 takes req.body.avatarUrl from an unauthenticated route, and server.js:11 only checks startsWith("https://") before server.js:14 calls axios.get(url) with default redirect following, so internal HTTPS hosts and redirects are reachable and the response size is returned at server.js:15.
